counterfactual_missing_items: No candidate other than R5 directly identifies the sacrococcygeal mass as the primary diagnosis
R3, R2, and R4 describe complications (bleeding, anemia, respiratory distress) without addressing the underlying mass
C1 is a redundant completion of R5, adding only the Altman type already present in R5's span
decisive_items: a 34×28 mm sacrococcygeal mass with internal and external components
MRI demonstrated a 60×70×57 mm sacrococcygeal mass with mixed features—predominantly solid with a 40 mm cyst—and no invasion or compression of pelvic structures or the coccyx (Altman type II)
response.rationale: R5 is the only candidate that directly answers the question by identifying the sacrococcygeal teratoma from the imaging findings. The other candidates describe secondary effects (hemorrhagic shock, anemia, respiratory distress) but do not provide the primary diagnosis. C1 is an append-only completion of R5 and adds no new diagnostic information beyond the Altman type already included in R5's raw support.

rejected.why: Describes hemorrhagic shock, a complication of the teratoma, but not the underlying diagnosis; lacks any reference to the sacrococcygeal mass.
Anemia is a consequence of bleeding, not the primary diagnosis; no mention of the mass.
Respiratory distress syndrome is a neonatal complication unrelated to the sacrococcygeal mass; no diagnostic link to the teratoma.
Redundant completion of R5, adding only the Altman type already present in R5's raw support; no independent diagnostic value.
